title: RAW_UNSCREENED: Bodennähe-Signatur gegen Höhenaufstieg
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: f77r contains repeated qotedy/qokaiin/qokeedy sequences and label/prose pairs; an Aristotle I.12-inspired near-ground freezing reading predicts a distinct local signature against an upper-air ascent account.

design.scope_description: Only already exposed f77r text/labels and cached Aristotle I.9-12 source; no new image or selector.
design.mechanism: Near-ground reading ties sudden state change to short descent/close endpoint; rival places formation in an upper region before descent.
design.unit: Exact whole-form sequences at named f77r loci.
design.prediction: Near-ground reading predicts large/abrupt state or endpoint forms immediately after a compact cloud/water sequence; upper-air reading predicts an explicit high/upper transition before the endpoint and a longer descent relation.
concrete_observations: Aristotle I.12 contrasts near-ground hail formation with the rejected cloud-thrust-up theory; GDT932 supplies f77r.14-15 and .27/.42 sequences with qok/qot and qokeedy forms.
linked_consequences: The near-ground model requires a local abrupt state-to-endpoint order; upper-air model requires a written elevation/upper-region cue before descent.
design.distinguishing_observation: Search only the already exposed f77r order/neighbor classes for a predeclared elevation cue versus abrupt endpoint; absence of a cue is not positive evidence.
design.strongest_likely_failure: No f77r token is independently known as height, hail, cloud or endpoint, so the historical contrast may have no usable manuscript realization.
